anomalies.observed: On the right-hand side of the schematic the node on the cathode side of D2 (the servo power rail that also feeds C1-C4 and J3 pin 2 / J8 pin 2) is wired to BOTH pin 1 and pin 2 of each 3-pin servo header. The vertical green wire at the left edge of J3/J8 that comes from below D2 branches into the pin-1 and pin-2 rows of both connectors; there is no GND symbol or GND wire on J3 pin 1 or J8 pin 1 (the only GND symbols in that area are the bottoms of C1-C4).
anomalies.expected: A standard 3-pin hobby/serial servo header carries GND on pin 1, +V on pin 2 and signal on pin 3. The spec states D2 feeds the servo rail 'before reaching J3/J8 pin 2' and that 'Pin 3 is the signal pin', so pin 1 must be GND. Pin 1 should therefore be connected to GND, not to the +5V servo rail.

evidence.quote: D2 PMEG3030EP 3A 360mV ... cathode node joins C1/C2/C3/C4 tops and the two upper wires of J3 and J8 (page 1, right side)
a second diode D2 (PMEG3030EP, annotated "3A 360mV" in the schematic ... feeds a dedicated servo power rail backed by four 100 µF capacitors (C1–C4) before reaching J3/J8 pin 2
J3, J8 ... Servo header ... Pin 3 is the signal pin

anomalies.impact: The ground pin of both servo connectors is shorted to the +5V servo rail and no ground is provided to the headers. Plugging in an SG90/RS304MD servo ties its brown (GND) lead to +5V, so the servo sees no supply voltage and its internal ground net sits at +5V; the servo will not operate and a large shoot-through current is likely when plugged in, risking damage to the servo and the D2/+5V supply.

parsed.summary: The schematic matches the spec in component identities, values and the PWM/serial jumper topology, but the servo headers appear mis-wired: J3 pin 1 and J8 pin 1 (the ground pins) are tied to the +5V servo power rail instead of to GND, leaving the servo connectors without a ground pin and shorting their GND lead to +5V.
